Detailed Description

MNE-CPP: reading, processing, source estimation and acquisition of MEG/EEG data in standard C++.

Every library shares this namespace; the class names carry their library prefix (FiffInfo, BidsChannel, MnaProject, ...). The Qt-based display libraries live in mne::disp.

Stable error codes. Values are part of the ABI and are never renumbered.

Success.

No data (reader) or no space (output writer) within the timeout.

EndOfStream 

The producer finished and every committed sample has been read.

Overrun 

The producer overwrote samples while a view was held; discard the view's data.

DeviceStopped 

The source was stopped while waiting.

Late 

An output sample, event or segment targets a sample the device has already played.

NotSynchronized 

The streams are not phase-locked in one clock domain, or the reference was lost.

BeforeStart 

The mapped instant precedes sample 0 of the target stream.

The instant is not on the target's schedulable grid (sampleAlignment); check the clock setup.

InvalidUri 

The URI does not have the form scheme://target?key=value.

UnknownScheme 

No backend is registered for the URI scheme.

InvalidParameter 

A URI or configuration parameter is unknown or out of range.

BackendUnavailable 

A runtime-loaded library (BrainFlow, liblsl, vendor SDK) was not found.

UnsupportedVersion 

A runtime-loaded library has a version outside the supported range.

DeviceNotFound 

The device, file or network endpoint does not exist or does not answer.

DeviceIo 

The device or file failed during acquisition or output.

InvalidState 

The call is not allowed in the current state.

UnsupportedFormat 

The sample format or layout cannot be used for this operation.

ShapeMismatch 

A caller-owned buffer has the wrong shape.

TooManyReaders 

All reader slots of the stream are in use.

InvalidBuffer 

An adopted external buffer is misaligned or not a power of two in samples.

OutOfMemory 

The ring or its memory lock could not be allocated.

PlatformUnsupported 

The backend or option is not available on this platform.

WrongDirection 

A writer was requested for an input stream, or a gating reader for an input stream.

WriterInUse 

The output stream already has its writer.

DeviceMemory 

The samples live in GPU memory, which the CPU must not read or write.

NotSupported 

The device does not offer this function (e.g. impedance measurement).

PermissionDenied 

The operating system refused the request (e.g. a realtime priority without the right).

Internal 

Invariant violation inside mne_acq; please report it.

Memory layout of a ring.

Planar

◆ annotateAmplitude()

DSPSHARED_EXPORT mne::FiffAnnotations mne::annotateAmplitude ( const Eigen::MatrixXd & data,
const mne::FiffInfo & info,
double sfreq,
const AnnotateAmplitudeParams & params,
mne::StringList * bads = nullptr )

Annotate spans where consecutive samples jump or stay flat, as mne.preprocessing.annotate_amplitude.

For every data channel that is not bad, the absolute differences between consecutive samples are compared with params.peak (at least) and params.flat (at most); runs shorter than params.dMinDuration are ignored. A channel whose runs cover at least params.dBadPercent of the recording is returned in bads; the runs of the other channels are merged into "BAD_flat" and "BAD_peak" annotations. Unlike mne, a channel that is bad for both reasons is listed once, and BAD_ACQ_SKIP spans are not skipped (the data matrix carries no annotations).

Parameters
[in]dataRaw data matrix (n_channels × n_times).
[in]infoMeasurement info (channel types, names and bads).
[in]sfreqSampling frequency in Hz.
[in]paramsThresholds; at least one of peak and flat must be set.
[out]badsIf not null, receives the channels annotated for too long, in channel order.
Returns
"BAD_flat" and "BAD_peak" annotations.

◆ annotateMusclZscore()

DSPSHARED_EXPORT mne::FiffAnnotations mne::annotateMusclZscore ( const Eigen::MatrixXd & data,
const mne::FiffInfo & info,
double sfreq,
const AnnotateMusclParams & params = AnnotateMusclParams(),
Eigen::RowVectorXd * scores = nullptr )

Detect muscle artifacts via high-frequency z-score and annotate bad segments.

Algorithm of mne.preprocessing.annotate_muscle_zscore with ch_type None:

  1. Pick the magnetometers, else the gradiometers, else the EEG channels.
  2. Band-pass them with mne's default FIR filter (FirFilter::filterData).
  3. Take the Hilbert envelope (FFT length padded to the next 5-smooth size).
  4. Z-score every channel over time, sum over channels and divide by sqrt(n_channels).
  5. Low-pass the score at 4 Hz with the same FIR filter.
  6. Mark samples above the threshold; good stretches shorter than dMinLengthGood become bad.
Parameters
[in]dataRaw data matrix (n_channels × n_times).
[in]infoMeasurement info.
[in]sfreqSampling frequency in Hz.
[in]paramsDetection parameters.
[out]scoresIf not null, receives the smoothed score per sample (mne's scores_muscle).
Returns
FiffAnnotations with "BAD_muscle" entries.

Project a source estimate to the sensors, as mne.apply_forward.

A free-orientation forward is first converted to fixed orientation along the (patch-averaged) cortical normals. The source estimate rows are matched to forward columns by vertex number per hemisphere (stc.nVerticesLh splits lh and rh); a vertex the forward lacks is an error. Repair stimulus artifacts by interpolating or zeroing data around events.

For each event sample, the data in the window [event + tmin_samples, event + tmax_samples] is either linearly interpolated from the boundary values or set to zero.

Parameters

[in]eventsEvent matrix (Nx3: [sample, before, after]). Only the sample column (col 0) is used to locate artifact windows.
[in]sfreqSampling frequency in Hz.
[in]eventIdIf >= 0, only process events where column 2 (after) matches this value. If < 0, process all events. Default: -1.
[in]tminStart of artifact window in seconds relative to event (negative = before event). Default: 0.0 (event onset).
[in]tmaxEnd of artifact window in seconds relative to event. Default: 0.01 (10 ms after event).
[in]modeRepair mode (Linear interpolation or zero-padding). Default: StimArtifactMode::Linear.

bool projection = false )

Re-reference EEG channels to average, specific channel(s), or REST.

Only modifies rows of good EEG channels (kind == FIFFV_EEG_CH, not in info.bads), as mne.set_eeg_reference does. Bad and non-EEG channels are left untouched.

Parameters
[in,out]dataData matrix (n_channels x n_times). Modified in-place.
[in,out]infoMeasurement info (identifies EEG channels; receives the projector).
[in]refChannelsReference channel name(s).
  • Empty or "average" -> average reference (mean of all good EEG channels).
  • Single channel name -> re-reference to that channel.
  • Multiple channel names -> re-reference to mean of those channels.
[in]projectionAverage reference only: append an inactive average-reference projector over the good EEG channels to info.projs (mne make_eeg_average_ref_proj) and leave the data unchanged. Nothing is added if one is already present.

◆ tokenize()

INVSHARED_EXPORT std::vector< InvToken > mne::tokenize ( const InvSourceEstimate & estimate,
const InvTokenizeOptions & options = InvTokenizeOptions() )

Serialise an InvSourceEstimate into a flat token sequence.

Converts the full multimodal content of an InvSourceEstimate (grid amplitudes, positions, couplings, focal dipoles, connectivity matrices) into a linear sequence of InvToken elements. Each token carries a vocabulary ID and an optional continuous float value.

The options parameter controls which data layers are emitted and allows sub-sampling of dense grids to fit context-limited attention windows.

Parameters
[in]estimateThe source estimate to tokenize.
[in]optionsControls layer inclusion and sub-sampling (default: all layers, no sub-sampling).
Returns
A vector of InvToken representing the serialised estimate.
See also
fromTokens, InvTokenizeOptions, InvToken

Determines the origin of target from loop-back markers against reference and verifies the declared clock relation: every marker must imply the same origin within toleranceTicks, so drift (a missing or wrong clock connection) is detected instead of producing wrong samples.

Parameters
[in]targetTimebase to verify; same domain as reference, Declared or FrequencyLocked.
[in]markersObservations; at least 1 for FrequencyLocked, at least 2 spanning minSpanSamples for Declared.
[in]referencePhaseLocked timebase of the domain.
[in]toleranceTicksAllowed spread of the implied origins (edge detection jitter).
[in]minSpanSamplesMinimum distance in target samples between first and last marker for Declared.
Returns
The PhaseLocked target timebase (originUncertaintyTicks = observed spread), or NotSynchronized when the domains differ, the reference is not PhaseLocked, too few markers were given, or the implied origins drift by more than toleranceTicks.
